title: A Systematic Evaluation of Preference Aggregation in Federated RLHF for Pluralistic Alignment of LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model alignment and cross-group fairness by treating different countries as distinct user groups. The paper compares LLM preference probability predictions and rankings against country-specific survey data from the Pew Research Global Attitudes Surveys, calculating a Fairness Index (FI) and Minimum Alignment Scores to ensure no country's preferences are marginalized during reward aggregation.

Assessing how well the federated RLHF aggregation strategies represent diverse, group-level preferences on social, political, and economic issues without overfitting to a majority demographic, using distance-based (e.g., Wasserstein, KL Divergence) and ranking-based (e.g., Kendall Tau) reward metrics across different preference clusters.
